record.reasoning: Dates and the EO 12292 amendments check out, but the reason given for section 1-101 is contradicted by held sources. Section 1-101 makes payment of section 8(a)(2) additional compensation 'governed by the regulations contained in Executive Order No. 10000, as amended, which govern the payment of additional compensation in foreign areas (referred to as foreign post differential)'. The claim says EO 10000 'is itself still in the held record only as partially amended (EO 10261 revoked its section 404 and EO 10623 its sections 402 and 403)' and, in its member checks, that EO 10000 'remains in force as partially amended'. The held EO 10903 (January 9, 1961) section 5(a) revoked 'Parts I, III, IV, and V of Executive Order No. 10000'. Part I is 'Additional Compensation in Foreign Areas', the foreign post differential rules that section 1-101 points to. The same section also revoked EO 10261 and EO 10623 themselves. The claim's account of what survives of EO 10000, and so of what section 1-101 operates on, is wrong. The search for ends of the referenced regulations missed a held order.

defects.claim_says: EO 10000 is still in the held record only as partially amended (EO 10261 revoked its section 404 and EO 10623 its sections 402 and 403); no held order revokes EO 10000, which 'remains in force as partially amended', so section 1-101 is operative.
defects.source_says: Held EO 10903 (January 9, 1961), section 5(a), revokes 'Parts I, III, IV, and V of Executive Order No. 10000' together with EO 10261 and EO 10623 themselves. Part I is 'ADDITIONAL COMPENSATION IN FOREIGN AREAS', the very foreign-post-differential regulations section 1-101 incorporates. The claim does not mention this revocation or explain how section 1-101 operates on revoked regulations.

record.reasoning: The delegations in sections 1-102 and 1-103, the EO 12292 section 9 amendments (effective as of 1981-02-15) and the revocation of EO 10853 in section 1-104 all check out. But the claim says it resolved its EO 10000 dependency by reading the held EO 10000 context, and the held record contradicts it. EO 10903 revoked Part I of EO 10000, the part section 1-101 points to, plus the two amending orders the claim cites. The stated basis for section 1-101's continuing predicate is therefore factually wrong and incomplete. Reasons must match the sources, so the claim is rejected. The whole-order YES may still be right on the other clauses.

(a) Section 1— 102(c)(1) is amended by striking out “Section 911(9) of the 
Foreign Service Act of 1946, as amended (22 U.S.C. 1136(9))” and inserting in 
lieu thereof “Section 901(6) of the Foreign Service Act of 1980 (22 U.S.C. 
4081(6))”;
(b) Section 1-103 is amended by striking out “Foreign Service Act of 1946, as 
amended” and inserting in lieu thereof “Foreign Service Act of 1980”.
